title: 444. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Vertical Translation of a Trigonometric Graph
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the transformation produced by adding a constant to a sine function.
questions.question: How is the graph of \(y=\sin x+3\) obtained from the graph of \(y=\sin x\)?

options.label: B
options.text: Shift it \(3\) units to the right.

questions.explanation: Adding \(3\) outside the sine increases every \(y\)-value by \(3\), so every point moves \(3\) units up. A shift to the right would require replacing \(x\) by \(x-3\) inside the sine, giving \(y=\sin(x-3)\).
questions.hint: Ask whether the constant changes the output of the function or its input.

questions.learningObjective: Find the midline of a vertically translated cosine.
questions.question: What is the midline of \(y=\cos x-2\)?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(y=\cos x\) oscillates about \(y=0\). Subtracting \(2\) lowers every point by \(2\), so the new midline is \(y=-2\) and the graph oscillates between \(-3\) and \(-1\). The sign of the constant must be kept.
questions.hint: The midline moves by the same amount and in the same direction as every other point.

questions.learningObjective: Find the range of a vertically translated sine.
questions.question: What is the range of \(y=\sin x+3\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(-1\le\sin x\le 1\), adding \(3\) to each part gives \(2\le\sin x+3\le 4\). The lower bound is \(3-1=2\); the interval starting at \(3\) forgets that the sine also takes negative values.
questions.hint: Add the constant to both the smallest and the largest value of the sine.

questions.learningObjective: Find the maximum value of a vertically translated cosine.
questions.question: What is the maximum value of \(y=\cos x-2\)?
questions.explanation: The largest value of \(\cos x\) is \(1\), so the largest value of \(\cos x-2\) is \(1-2=-1\). The value \(-3=-1-2\) is the minimum of the function.
questions.hint: Start from the largest value of the cosine and apply the shift.

questions.learningObjective: Decide whether a vertically translated sine graph meets the x-axis.
questions.question: Does the graph of \(y=\sin x+3\) have any \(x\)-intercepts?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because its minimum value is \(2\), which is greater than \(0\).

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because every sine graph crosses the \(x\)-axis.

questions.explanation: An \(x\)-intercept requires \(\sin x+3=0\), that is, \(\sin x=-3\), which is impossible since \(\sin x\ge -1\). The graph stays between \(y=2\) and \(y=4\), entirely above the \(x\)-axis. Only sine graphs whose range contains \(0\) cross the axis.
questions.hint: Compare the range of the function with the value \(0\).

questions.concept: Writing a rule for a vertical shift
questions.learningObjective: Write the rule for a cosine graph translated vertically.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=2\cos x\) is shifted \(5\) units down. Which rule describes the new graph?
questions.explanation: A vertical shift changes the output, so \(5\) is subtracted from the whole expression: \(y=2\cos x-5\). The rule \(y=2\cos(x-5)\) changes the input and describes a shift of \(5\) units to the right.
questions.hint: A vertical shift is applied outside the cosine, to the value of the function.

questions.concept: The y-intercept of a translated sine
questions.learningObjective: Compute the y-intercept of a vertically translated sine.
questions.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\sin x-4\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(x=0\): \(y=\sin 0-4=0-4=-4\). The value \(-3\) would result from using \(\cos 0=1\) or the maximum of the function instead of the value at \(x=0\).
questions.hint: Substitute \(x=0\) and recall the value of \(\sin 0\).

questions.concept: Smallest shift that keeps a graph non-negative
questions.learningObjective: Determine the least upward shift for which a sine graph never goes below the x-axis.
questions.question: What is the smallest value of \(d\) for which \(\sin x+d\ge 0\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: The smallest value of \(\sin x+d\) is \(-1+d\). The condition \(-1+d\ge 0\) gives \(d\ge 1\), so the smallest possible value is \(d=1\). With \(d=1\) the graph touches the \(x\)-axis at its minimum points. The value \(d=2\) also works, but it is not the smallest.
questions.hint: Find the minimum value of the expression in terms of \(d\) and require it to be at least \(0\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve for the vertical shift that produces a given maximum value.
questions.question: The function \(y=3\sin x+d\) has maximum value \(1\). What is \(d\)?
questions.explanation: The maximum of \(3\sin x\) is \(3\), so the maximum of \(3\sin x+d\) is \(3+d\). Setting \(3+d=1\) gives \(d=-2\). Adding the amplitude to the maximum, \(1+3=4\), goes in the wrong direction.
questions.hint: Write the maximum value in terms of the amplitude and \(d\), then solve.

questions.concept: Features unchanged by a vertical shift
questions.learningObjective: Identify which features of a sinusoid change under a vertical translation.
questions.question: The graphs of \(y=4\sin(2x)\) and \(y=4\sin(2x)+7\) are compared. Which feature is different for the two graphs?
questions.explanation: Adding \(7\) moves every point up by \(7\), so the midline changes from \(y=0\) to \(y=7\) and the range changes from \([-4,4]\) to \([3,11]\). The amplitude \(4\) and the period \(\frac{2\pi}{2}=\pi\) are the same for both graphs, because a vertical shift does not stretch the graph.
questions.hint: A vertical translation moves a graph without changing its shape.
